h1:
Rice-Field & Canal Cafes
in Pathum Thani: 10 Spots
intro: Pathum Thani sits right next to Bangkok — just a few dozen minutes' drive away. But once you pass Rangsit toward Khlong Luang and Lam Luk Ka, you hit green rice fields and long stretches of canal. Lately a bunch of cafes have opened out in the fields and along the water. We've rounded up the ones that are actually open right now, with their area, rough prices, and opening hours so you can plan before you head out.

blocks.html: The appeal of Pathum Thani's cafes is that you can still find rice-field and waterside views this close to Bangkok. Most of the spots cluster in two zones: the Khlong Luang side (around Khlong 1–6 and along Sai Mai–Rangsit road) and the Lam Luk Ka side (Khlong 5 and beyond), where the fields are still wide open. Some places sit on real rice paddies planted by season; others are landscaped gardens along the canal. We picked 8 spots that get reviewed often and are genuinely open, ordered from the strongest field views on down.

blocks.text: 8 rice-field & canal cafes people actually go to

items.name: The Aileen Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe with rice-field views and a grove of sugar palms in Mueang Pathum Thani district. Bright pink tones, with both an air-conditioned zone and an outdoor area looking out over the open fields. It's one of the most photographed spots in the province for social media. It also does savory dishes like seafood fried rice and tom yum — not just coffee.
items.meta: Mueang Pathum Thani district · open 11:00–21:00, closed Mon · THB 101–250 per person

items.name: Lamer Homecraft Cafe
items.blurb: A modern homemade-style cafe tucked into the rice fields off Ratchaphruek–346 road on the Bang Luang side. Quiet, with corners to sit and catch the breeze over the fields. It serves drinks, cake, and made-to-order savory food — a good place to settle in for a long morning before the sun gets harsh.
items.meta: Mueang district (Bang Luang) · Mon–Fri 11:00–21:00, Sat–Sun 10:00–21:00 · drinks & bakery from 9:00

items.name: Nichromy Cafe
items.blurb: A green cafe along Khlong 5 in Lam Luk Ka. The draw is rice-field views plus several different waterside photo spots — Balinese bird's-nest pods, a deck looking over the fields, and netted gazebos by the canal. There's space for kids to run around, so it works for families.
items.meta: Lam Luk Ka district (Khlong 5) · Tue–Fri 8:00–18:00, Sat–Sun 8:00–20:00, closed Mon

items.name: The Kottage Cafe
items.blurb: A white English-country-style cafe out in the rice fields around Lat Lum Kaeo. Roomy, airy seating that looks out over the paddies in a long line — good for anyone who likes a clean, minimal white look set against the green of the fields.
items.meta: Lat Lum Kaeo district · rice-field view · coffee, bakery & light bites

items.name: Nitan Cafe & Garden
items.blurb: A cafe done up in English country-garden style, with a small stream running through the garden and a lawn area for kids to play. The drinks and desserts are named after storybook characters, and the shady setting suits an unhurried, chill afternoon.
items.meta: Khlong Luang–Lam Luk Ka area · garden & stream · family-friendly

items.name: Prem Cafe In the Garden
items.blurb: A nature-focused cafe ringed by all kinds of trees, with a waterside zone for catching the breeze. Prices are easy on the wallet — a good pick if you just want green canalside surroundings without paying a lot.
items.meta: Pathum Thani area · waterside zone · easy prices

items.name: Rueun Pla Too Cafe
items.blurb: A waterside cafe that sells fresh fish dishes alongside drinks. Good for a canalside lunch when you want a proper savory meal and a seat with water views — not just sipping coffee.
items.meta: Pathum Thani area · canalside · fish & savory dishes

items.name: Farm Cafe and Restaurant
items.blurb: A cafe on a farm with sheep you can photograph and feed — good for bringing kids. It has drinks, desserts, and food, and it's a stop kids tend to enjoy more than a regular cafe, even though the view is more farm than open rice field.
items.meta: Pathum Thani area · sheep farm · good for young kids

items.name: Na Pathum Cafe
items.blurb: A countryside-style cafe on Route 347 with an actual miniature train that loops around the rice paddies and through a sugar-palm grove — 60 baht buys you two laps, and kids are all over it. A long wooden boardwalk stretches out into the field for photos, prettiest when the rice is green or in the cool season. The menu goes well beyond coffee: Wongnai reviewers rate the noodles, Thai som tam and the pandan young-coconut cake, so the whole family eats well.
items.meta: Ban Klang, Mueang Pathum Thani (Route 347) · Open 10:00–19:00

items.name: Kanya Cafe
items.blurb: An open-air cafe-restaurant hybrid right off Route 346 in Bang Luang, facing a wide stretch of rice paddies. Seating comes in every flavor — triangular pavilions at the field's edge, hammocks, and Japanese-style floor tables beside a koi pond. Reviewers tend to pair drinks with the Thai-Isan kitchen; the dishes people talk about are the seafood hor mok served in young coconut, fried sea bass with fish sauce, and coconut cake. There's live music on weekends, and pets are welcome.
items.meta: Bang Luang, Mueang Pathum Thani (Route 346/Ratchaphruek Rd) · Open 10:00–20:00

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The rice fields in Pathum Thani are greenest from early to mid rainy season (roughly June–September), while the golden ripening-grain stretch falls in late rainy season into early cool season. If you want the fields at their lushest green, call the cafe first to ask how the paddies are looking this round — some spots are real fields that get harvested by season.

blocks.text: Pick by zone: Khlong Luang vs Lam Luk Ka

blocks.html: These two zones feel a little different. The Khlong Luang side (including nearby Bang Luang and Lat Lum Kaeo) is easy to reach from Rangsit and Don Muang, so it's good for a stop along the way. The Lam Luk Ka side, Khlong 5 and up, still has wider fields and more canalside spots — better for a day when you mean to drive out and settle in for a while.

items.name: Khlong Luang–Bang Luang zone
items.blurb: Close to Rangsit and Don Muang, easy to reach, good for a stop along the way. Both field cafes and waterside gardens, like Lamer Homecraft and The Aileen.

items.name: Lam Luk Ka Khlong 5+ zone
items.blurb: Wide fields and lots of canalside, good for a day you mean to settle in for. Plenty of water-view spots and varied photo corners, like Nichromy.

blocks.text: Make the most of a Pathum Thani field cafe

items: Go in the morning or evening — midday sun over the fields is harsh and hot, and the outdoor zones get hard to sit in. Before 11am or after 3pm the light is nicer and it's not too hot.
Check closing days first — many Pathum Thani cafes close on Monday or Tuesday, and some open later on Saturday–Sunday than on weekdays. A quick call is the safest bet.

A car is by far the easiest — most spots are down canalside lanes or out in the fields where public transport doesn't reach. If you don't have a car, use a ride-hailing app from a Red Line station or Rangsit.
Allow extra time for parking — field cafes often have dirt lots that can get muddy in the rain. Shoes you don't mind getting messy will be more comfortable.

faq.q: Where are the rice-field cafes in Pathum Thani?
faq.a: They cluster in two main zones: the Khlong Luang–Bang Luang–Lat Lum Kaeo side, which is easy to reach from Rangsit and Don Muang, and the Lam Luk Ka Khlong 5 side and beyond, where the fields are still wide and there are plenty of canalside spots.

faq.q: Which Pathum Thani cafe has the best rice-field views and photos?
faq.a: The Aileen Cafe in the city district is known for its field views, sugar-palm grove, and pink corners. Lamer Homecraft and Nichromy Cafe also have several photo spots along the fields and canal.

faq.q: When are the rice fields greenest at Pathum Thani's field cafes?
faq.a: The fields are at their deepest green from early to mid rainy season, roughly June to September, while the golden ripening-grain stretch runs from late rainy season into early cool season. It's worth calling the cafe first, since some are real paddies harvested by season.

faq.q: Can you reach Pathum Thani's field cafes by public transport?
faq.a: Most sit down canalside lanes or out in the fields where public transport doesn't reach, so a car is easiest. If you don't have one, use a ride-hailing app from a Red Line station or Rangsit.

faq.q: Which Pathum Thani cafes serve savory food, not just coffee?
faq.a: The Aileen Cafe has seafood fried rice and tom yum, Lamer Homecraft does made-to-order savory dishes, and Rueun Pla Too focuses on canalside fish dishes — all good for a proper lunch.
